records.text: A creature of living stone, this elemental bears the form of rock.

Gorn directs the Horde effort in Kargath to recover the Sign of the Earth after Tho'grun's betrayal, then use it to free and kill Blacklash and Hematus. He regards the ogres' betrayal and the drakes' old alliance with Deathwing as dishonorable threats to the Horde.
Sranda is a light armor and weapons merchant who also repairs equipment, a practical outfitter for travelers seeking gear and repairs.
A Dustbelcher Ogre who answers a challenge with blunt threats to smash the one who stands against it.
A Dustbelcher Brute who answers a challenge with blunt threats to smash the one who stands against it.
Dustbelcher Wyrmhunters are crude brutes who roar that they will smash and crush their foes, and they hurl boulders.
Dustbelcher Maulers threaten to smash and crush opponents when attacking.
Dustbelcher Shamans threaten to smash and crush opponents when attacking.
Dustbelcher Lords are crude brutes who roar that they will smash and crush their foes, and they bellow battle shouts.
Dustbelcher Ogre Mages threaten to smash and crush opponents when attacking.
Stone Golems are elemental golems made of stone.
A Scalding Whelp is a young dragonkin that hurls fireballs at its foes.
A Scorched Guardian is a dragonkin that breathes flame at its foes.
A Ridge Huntress is a beast.
The Ridge Stalker Patriarch is a beast in its local population.
A lesser rock elemental found in the surrounding region.
A greater rock elemental found across several areas of the surrounding region, stronger than the lesser rock elemental.
A Shadowforge Tunneler is a dwarf who fights from a defensive stance with armor-breaking strikes; badly hurt, it flees to find help.
A Shadowforge darkweaver who fights with Shadow Bolt, this dwarf is part of the Shadowforge presence in the area.
A Shadowforge Chanter is a spellcaster who shields itself with Power Word: Shield in a fight.
A Shadowforge Warrior is a dwarf melee fighter who spins into a whirlwind of blows.
A high-ranking Shadowforge commander, this dwarf joins a fight with Devotion Aura.

An elemental called Ambassador Infernus, sent by Ragnaros to Angor Fortress to oversee the Shadowforge search for lost artifacts in Uldaman. Advisor Belgrum describes the search as a growing threat to Ironforge.
A large siege golem, an elemental construct, found in several parts of the Badlands, including Angor Fortress. Badly wounded, it unleashes a desperate spell.
A war golem found in the Badlands, including Angor Fortress and the nearby ruins. This powerful elemental construct uses a spell when injured.
A powerful elemental known as a Rumbler, found in the Badlands around the Arathi Highlands border. It can unleash a ground tremor while fighting.
Barnabus is a beast of the Badlands, found around the Valley of Fangs; once wounded, it turns to a special attack.
Anathemus is a powerful giant found in the Valley of Fangs in the Badlands. It fights with special attacks and turns to another when wounded.

Once associated with the Twilight's Hammer, Theldurin now fears what the Scroll of Myzrael could unleash. He works to repair its fragments, hoping to use it to contain Myzrael again, and speaks in anxious, fragmented warnings about a coming doom. He calls himself mad, but remains focused on stopping the danger.
A hostile rock elemental that becomes more dangerous as it is wounded, its enrage driving it into a frenzy.

Rigglefuzz is a goblin tinkerer and cook in the Badlands. He developed flash bombs from crushed blue pearls to deter the region’s wildlife, and asks for pearls to keep making them. He also cooks spicy barbecued buzzard wings and studies the power stones found at Uldaman; after the Shadowforge dwarves expelled him from Angor Fortress, he sought stones for himself.

Sigrun Ironhew learned a distinctive fiery weapon-enchantment technique as an apprentice to Feranor Steeltoe, though she keeps its process partly secret. After the Uldaman excavation evacuation, she works to feed and equip the camp, gather scrap metal for defenses, and awaits word from Ironforge or the Explorers' League.
Gorrik is a Wind Rider Master who offers fast travel. When attacked, he calls for the grunts and summons an enraged wyvern.

Garek is an agent of Krasus and the Kirin Tor, sent on a vital assignment in Lethlor Ravine whose details he keeps secret. He seeks the Sign of the Earth, stolen by ogres, and works to release and then destroy the imprisoned dragon lieutenants Blacklash and Hematus. He knows the Sign was made by the Dark Iron dwarves to bind the twins and plans to report his success to Krasus.
A Stonevault spellcaster, the Seer hurls lightning bolts at its foes.
A Stonevault Bonesnapper strikes and pummels its foes and flees to find help when badly wounded. Bonesnappers are hunted in the search for Agmond's killer, Murdaloc.
A Stonevault shaman who uses a Healing Ward while injured.
A Dustbelcher warrior who announces its intent to smash or crush its foe when combat begins. Its blunt threats fit its role as a direct frontline fighter among the Dustbelcher.
A Dustbelcher mystic with the same blunt battle cries as its kin, promising to smash or crush its foe, who also hurls lightning bolts.
Grawl is a general-goods merchant who offers goods for browsing.

Prospector Ryedol is an Explorers' League prospector whose excavation work was tied to the search for Uldaman's lost artifacts. His boss Hammertoe Grez worked closely with Historian Karnik. Shadowforge Dark Irons attacked the dig site and killed nearly everyone there; Ryedol escaped with his life but lost his lucky pick. He fears the Dark Irons took Hammertoe to learn about the titan excavations and golem research, and learning that Hammertoe is dead deepens his grief; he wants Hammertoe's life work and death to count for something.

Lucien Tosselwrench works with Lotwil Veriatus in the Badlands and has been learning from Lotwil’s scientific research. Alongside that collaboration, Lucien develops potions and makes enchanted bracers from materials gathered for Lotwil’s work. He asks for healing and invisibility potions because he worries they may soon be needed if Lotwil’s latest invention goes badly. When Lotwil’s experiment is underway, Lucien watches him nervously and says he will stay behind cover, inviting the adventurer to join him there.

Lotwil Veriatus is a mage researching elemental binding in the Badlands. He is developing shackles to let mages summon more powerful elementals, combining alchemy, engineering, and arcane work. His requests for elemental materials and other components support a project he calls his top priority, though his repeated assurances that it is nearly finished suggest the work is taking longer than he claims. He tests his design himself, and one test gets out of control. Servo assists him, while Lotwil also addresses Lucien during the work.

Servo is Lotwil Veriatus's mechanical assistant in the Badlands. He checks and handles gizmos and research materials, and is loyal and protective: he promises to help guard his master and calls for Lotwil's protection. Servo wonders where the trees have gone and says that one day he will be a real boy, giving him an individual, wistful manner. He also remarks on the Badlands' dry heat.
An ogre mercenary who once worked with his band for the Horde, Tho'grun betrayed his employers and took the Sign of the Earth for himself. The Horde now seeks to recover it.
Murdaloc is named as Agmond's killer: the dying dwarf scrawled the name in the Badlands sandstone beside his own hand. A local order calls for his death.

Martek is an exiled smith living in a Badlands camp. Fizzle Brassbolts trusts his knowledge of metal to help develop stronger engine pistons, and Martek tests indurium flakes for heat resistance. He says Fizzle and his brother are among the few people who do not want him dead, giving his willingness to help a personal edge.
A Shadowforge Surveyor is a dungeon combatant that keeps Frost Armor ready outside combat.

Neeka Bloodscar is Kargath's head scout, responsible for keeping its outpost in contact with Stonard. She is wary of inexperienced outrunners and describes the Badlands as harsh; crag coyotes that raid Kargath's food stores are among the threats she directs people to hunt. She prepares reports for Helgrum the Swift in Stonard.
Stonevault bashers flee to seek assistance when badly injured.

Jarkal Mossmeld is a troll alchemical researcher and magical translator. Jarkal seeks magenta fungus caps and dragon blood, offering restorative elixirs or recipes in return. For a necklace from Uldaman, Jarkal translates a human journal and emphasizes the missing power source, aiming to profit from extra necklaces while leaving Droffers and Son Salvage unaware.

Thorkaf Dragoneye teaches Dragonscale Leatherworking in the Badlands. He treats the specialization as a serious commitment: his student must provide scorpid armor and dragonkin scales, and agree not to learn Elemental or Tribal Leatherworking. He presents the craft as a rewarding path and offers further training in the techniques the student has yet to learn.
A Kargath Grunt is a humanoid associated with the Kargath outpost in the Badlands.

Warlord Goretooth commands the Kargath Expeditionary Force. He wants the Dark Iron forces in Blackrock Depths destroyed, blaming them for the massacre of the 109th division, and demands that General Angerforge be brought to justice. He also orders the leaders of Blackrock Spire slain and important documents recovered. A decisive, mission-focused commander, he ties the reconnaissance division's findings to strikes on Dark Iron officials.

Shadowmage Vivian Lagrave is a Forsaken researcher with the Kargath Expeditionary Force. She seeks the Darkstone Tablet’s old alchemical writings for study and wants the Thunderbrew recipe sent to the Apothecarium, hoping its virtues might serve Forsaken objectives. Her dry amusement at the idea of using the ale against the Alliance hints at her allegiance and outlook.

Hierophant Theodora Mulvadania investigates the machines imported into the Searing Gorge. She collects elemental shards from Burning Steppes automatons to determine their origin, then recognizes the G.L.A. initials and rank markings and sends a sample to elemental scholar Lotwil Veriatus for help. Her careful examination shows a methodical approach to the investigation.

Lexlort is an intelligence and field-logistics operative of the Kargath Expeditionary Force. He tracked Grark Lorkrub, accusing him of passing operational information to the Blackrock orcs, and arranged for Grark's custody transfer with Thorium Shackles at the Searing Gorge rendezvous. He also directs the search for Bijou, whom he says diverted Horde funds while working with Kibler, and wants her returned alive with her reports.

Galamav the Marksman serves with the Kargath Expeditionary Force. He recounts how an arrow killed Gargal and carried a note bearing Commander Gor'shak's signature, directing the search for Gor'shak in Blackrock Depths while warning that it may be a trap. He also assigns the strike against Halycon, the Blackrock worgs' pack mistress, as a step toward thinning the Spire's worg sentries.

Thal'trak Proudtusk serves the Kargath Expeditionary Force but cannot leave his post to search for his missing wife, Sha'ni. He rejects Goretooth's advice to move on and asks others to learn her fate. They had planned to move to the Hinterlands after her final mission. When her wedding nose-ring returns, he collapses in grief and rejects it as meaningless without her.
Razal'blade belongs to the Kargath Expeditionary Force.

Thunderheart investigates elemental disharmony at Blackrock Mountain for the Kargath Expeditionary Force, following the threat from Pyron to Lord Incendius and an unknown master. Reading the Tablet of Kurniya brings the name Ragnaros and fear of a new sundering. Thunderheart urges caution and believes Kargath must reconsider whether to stay and fight or flee.
Amakkar is an initiate of the Kargath Expeditionary Force.
Grunt Gargal is a Kargath Expeditionary Force grunt stationed in the Burning Steppes.

Sha'ni Proudtusk survived the slaughter of her platoon and Krom'Grul's captivity in the Burning Steppes. He took her wedding nose-ring, and she asks for him to be killed and the ring returned to her husband, Thal'trak. Her account of their planned life after their tours shows what she has lost.
Jazzrik sells blacksmithing supplies to anyone who comes by.
Innkeeper Shul'kar welcomes weary travelers to rest and share battle stories. Visitors can find lodging, food and seasonal treats.
Greth is a stable master who can stable a visitor's pet or help recover a lost companion.

7:XT is a long-distance recovery unit: an armored, non-humanoid construct that scans for life forms and resumes its search pattern when a target is lost. Its terse status reports describe its search behavior.

Advisor Sarophas is an exacting, status-conscious expedition member who is appalled by Kargath and its residents. After Dark Iron dwarves rob him, he asks for help recovering his clothes and rapier, saying he felt naked without his blade. Once reunited with his belongings, he thanks the people who helped him, while still calling them “the little people.”

The Badlands Flame Keeper tends the local festival fire and urges visitors to honor Horde flames across the lands. The keeper also voices hostility toward Alliance festival fires, encouraging their desecration. Its festival welcome and counsel reflect the factional rivalry surrounding the celebrations.

A small fire spirit and emissary to the elemental spirits, the Festival Scorchling is associated with the festival fires beside Horde settlements. Its dialogue welcomes incense as precious fuel and describes the energy it gains from it. It also boasts of being Ragnaros’s herald and threatening mortals, then says it was merely jesting.

place_records.text: You are in the Badlands, a harsh region of the Eastern Kingdoms. The Horde holds it in places, chiefly at Kargath, its main settlement. Crag coyotes, rock elementals, Dustbelcher ogres and Shadowforge dwarves are the dangers here.

You are in Apocryphan's Rest, a stretch of the Badlands where giant buzzards, ridge stalker patriarchs and elder crag coyotes hunt. A siege golem, a powerful elemental construct, is found here, and it can unleash a spell when badly wounded.

You are in Angor Fortress, a Shadowforge stronghold in the Badlands. Shadowforge warriors, chanters and commanders hold its halls, with stone golems and ridge stalkers nearby. A siege golem is found here too, and it can unleash a spell when badly wounded.

You are in Lethlor Ravine, where scalding whelps and scorched guardians haunt the ground. Black dragons have taken up residence here, and the drakes Blacklash and Hematus are kept imprisoned by runestones that may not hold. Garek, an agent of Krasus of the Kirin Tor, is here on a secret errand.

You are in Kargath, the Horde's main settlement in the Badlands, where the Kargath Expeditionary Force is based. Warlord Goretooth commands the force, and Neeka Bloodscar, its head scout, says crag coyotes raid the food stores. Gorn directs the effort to recover the Sign of the Earth, which ogres stole, and it has an inn and a stable.
You are in Camp Kosh, a Badlands camp where Dustbelcher warriors and mystics gather. Its ogres have been picking over the wagons and crates the Uldaman dig crew abandoned on the road.
You are in Camp Boff, where Dustbelcher ogres and brutes roam among feral crag coyotes and ridge huntresses. Buzzards circle overhead, and wandering ogres are sometimes seen here.
You are in Camp Wurg, a Badlands camp where Dustbelcher ogres and brutes roam with elder crag coyotes and ridge huntresses.
You are in Camp Cagg, a Dustbelcher camp where greater rock elementals, maulers, wyrmhunters and shamans gather. Tho'grun, who betrayed the Horde's efforts in Kargath, is among them.

You are in Agmond's End, where Stonevault bonesnappers and shamans, along with crag coyotes and rock elementals, make the ground dangerous. Theldurin the Lost is here, once tied to the Twilight's Hammer and fearful of what the Scroll of Myzrael could unleash.
You are in Hammertoe's Digsite, a Badlands dig where Shadowforge tunnelers and darkweavers are the dangers. A chalk message scrawled on the site's map says Hammertoe Grez was being taken to Uldaman.
You are in Dustbelch Grotto, a cave in the Badlands where Dustbelcher ogre mages and lords hold ground alongside greater rock elementals.

You are in Valley of Fangs, a Badlands valley where crag coyotes and ridge huntresses roam. Rigglefuzz, a goblin tinkerer and cook, makes flash bombs to scare off wildlife and studies power stones. Martek the Exiled, an exiled smith, lives in a camp here, and Jazzrik sells blacksmithing supplies.

You are in The Dustbowl, a Badlands ground where neutral folk work. Lotwil Veriatus, a mage, is researching elemental binding here with his mechanical assistant Servo, while Lucien Tosselwrench makes potions and enchanted bracers beside him. Lesser rock elementals, ridge huntresses, ridge stalkers and giant buzzards roam the area.
You are in Mirage Flats, in the Badlands. Crag coyotes, rock elementals and ridge huntresses roam the flats, and a long-distance recovery unit named 7:XT searches the open ground for life forms.
You are in The Maker's Terrace, a terrace in the Badlands. Shadowforge surveyors, diggers and ruffians work the ground here, with crag coyotes and a war golem among them.
You are in Dustwind Gulch, a gulch in the Badlands. Ridge stalkers, rabid crag coyotes and starving buzzards prowl it, and stonevault seers and bashers are found here too.
